title: Competing Orders Driven by Wigner Crystal Phase in Rhombohedral Graphene
authors: Zekang Zhou, Kilian Krötzsch, Raphaël Ayache, Yonggen Li, Sandeep Joy, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Moty Heiblum, Preden Roulleau, Mitali Banerjee
abstract: Rhombohedral graphene systems provide a unique platform where strong electronic interactions and nontrivial band topology coexist at low carrier densities and high displacement fields, giving rise to a rich landscape of emergent electronic phases. Here, we report that the highly insulating state on the low-density side of chiral superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene (R5G) corresponds to a Wigner crystal (WC) phase. In addition, a hole-doped metallic Wigner crystal (h-mWC) phase emerges near the WC boundary. Under an out-of-plane magnetic field, the system hosts competing magnetic-field-stabilized superconductivity (fSC) and unconventional reentrant quantum Hall (RIQH) states. These emergent phases are closely connected to the underlying WC and mWC states and evolve continuously across phase boundaries. Our results establish that WC phase plays an important role in the phase diagram of rhombohedral multilayer graphene and highlight its connection to a rich landscape of emergent phases.
summary: This work investigates the rich phase diagram of rhombohedral graphene, demonstrating that strong electron interactions drive the system into a Wigner Crystal (WC) state at low carrier densities. Under magnetic fields, this WC phase competes with superconducting and unconventional Quantum Hall states, establishing the WC's central role in governing these emergent correlated electronic orders.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the complex, emergent electronic phases arising from strong electron-electron interactions in rhombohedral graphene.
main_result: The highly insulating state at low carrier density is identified as a Wigner Crystal (WC) phase, which coexists and competes with superconducting (fSC) and reentrant quantum Hall (RIQH) states under magnetic fields.
method: Transport measurements, including $n-D$ maps of resistance ($	ext{R}_{xx}, 	ext{R}_{xy}$), differential conductance ($V-I$), and Landau fan diagrams, are used across varying magnetic fields and temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is rhombohedral multilayer graphene (specifically pentalayer graphene, R5G) encapsulated in hBN, allowing independent tuning of carrier density ($n$) and displacement field ($D$).
key_observables: Longitudinal resistance ($	ext{R}_{xx}$), Hall resistance ($	ext{R}_{xy}$), nonlinear $V-I$ characteristics, and quantized Hall plateaus.
important_parameters: Low carrier densities, out-of-plane magnetic fields ($B$), and the interplay between Coulomb interaction energy and kinetic energy.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping distinct phase boundaries (WC/mWC, cSC1, cSC2) observed through characteristic transport signatures like threshold behavior or sign reversals.
figures_summary: Figures map out $n-D$ phase diagrams showing regions corresponding to WC, $	ext{fSC}$, and $	ext{RIQH}$ states; Landau fan diagrams confirm the origin of these quantized/structured states from WC boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by varying carrier density ($n$) and displacement field ($D$), analyzing transport signatures (resistance, $V-I$ curves) at fixed magnetic fields to delineate competing orders like Wigner Crystals and superconductivity.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of strongly correlated insulating states (WC) coexisting with topological/superconducting phases in a tunable 2D material platform, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum phenomena.
